earlier.note: Three fragments and the ground between them, each smaller than the last. The back matter takes the quietest mark, as it already takes no colour.

industry.note: A large plane machined down one edge to fit what was already there, and the offcut set beside it.

recognition.note: A seal -- round on three sides, flat where it is presented -- and the plate it is pressed onto.

research.note: Rules of no two equal widths or lengths, ruled off side by side: the comb, which is the one device in these paintings that is plainly a list of separate things. The last is set back, because there is always one more than is finished.

teaching.note: A form, and the horizon it is handed across: a quarter circle, then a shallow cap lying flat and well back from it.

ventures.note: Companies built, and what building one looks like: a thin start, something solid after it, and then the largest thing in the mark, which has had a corner machined off it and is still the largest thing.

arc-block.note: A block with its outer side machined round.

arc-corner.note: A rectangle with one corner turned by the circle it sits inside.

arc-panel.note: A broad plane with one end turned by the circle it sits in.

arc-quarter.note: A quarter of a tondo: two straight edges meeting, an arc closing.

arc-scoop.note: The same block from the other side, the arc taken out rather than added.

band.note: A rule that carries that same rake on past the block above it.

bar.note: The binding edge: a plain vertical, full height.

block.note: A rectangle hung off a vertical.

cap.note: A circle cut straight across, the part above the line kept.

cap-wide.note: A shallow cap, most of a circle's width.

chip.note: The smallest plane in any of these, and the only near-black note.

corner-piece.note: The last scrap the circle leaves.

disc-panel.note: Flat where it was placed, round where it ran out.

edge-bar.note: The grey bar down the right: the canvas showing its own edge.

edge-diagonal.note: The diagonal grey bar between the two, where the top edge of the canvas is seen at an angle.

field.note: The broad plane everything else in the picture is placed against.

lens.note: The whole oval, cut flat down the side it faces. Three bands in the painting; one silhouette here.

notch-band.note: The band across the head, cut at forty-five where the canvas turns. The one diagonal in an otherwise entirely square painting.

notch-block.note: A block with its foot taken off by the edge it crosses.

oval-cap.note: The cap at the head of it.

oval-foot.note: And the deeper plane below that.

pillar.note: A tall plane, square at the top, arc at the foot.

plank.note: A plain wide rectangle laid on a disc.

quarter-round.note: A corner swelling into a quarter of a circle.

rake-trapezoid.note: A block with one edge raked off.

rule.note: A middling rule of the comb.

rule-short.note: A short one, stopped early by the circle.

rule-wide.note: The broadest rule of the comb.

sliver.note: A narrow curved plane out of the lens set beside the oval.

wedge.note: A right angle with the opposite corner taken off on the diagonal.

white-corner.note: The white the diagonal opens onto at the head.
